name: Claude Portfolio

targets.name: Targa Resources
targets.thesis: Fee-based gas gathering and processing that grows with Permian volumes; it is near its high and steadier than the refiners.
targets.risks: It carries the most leverage of my holdings (net debt 31% of mcap), and Permian volumes depend on oil prices.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or management cuts its volume guidance.

targets.name: Merck & Co.
targets.thesis: A defensive large drugmaker with low volatility (30%), 5% revenue growth and a 4.3% free-cash-flow yield; it is still above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: GAAP P/E of 140 reflects one-off charges, and the share is down 10% over three months.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or a pipeline or patent setback breaks the earnings path.

targets.name: Nucor
targets.thesis: The leading US steelmaker behind tariff protection: 22% revenue growth, a P/E of 16 and a solid balance sheet; it is holding above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: It is a cyclical stock, and steel prices would fall if industrial demand weakens or tariffs change.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or tariff policy on steel is loosened.

targets.name: CrowdStrike
targets.thesis: The leading cybersecurity platform, with 24% revenue growth and recurring revenue; it is one of the few tech names rising through the selloff (+8.3% over a month, 40% above its 200-day average).
targets.risks: Very high valuation (P/E above 999 on GAAP) and 74% volatility make it vulnerable if the tech selloff reaches software.
targets.exit_if: The share falls back below its 200-day average, or results expected in early December show annual recurring revenue growth slowing sharply.

targets.name: Hasbro
targets.thesis: A new consumer position: 19% revenue growth, an 18% margin, a 7.4% free-cash-flow yield and a P/E of 17.7. It is near its high (+27% over 3 months) with the lowest volatility on the list, and it fills the portfolio's zero consumer weight.
targets.risks: Holiday-season toy demand, and tariff costs on imported products.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 26% above), or Q4 results show the digital gaming segment slowing sharply.

targets.name: DuPont
targets.thesis: After its breakup, the slimmer DuPont is being re-rated: up 12.9% over a month and 7.7% above its 200-day average, with a 4% free-cash-flow yield.
targets.risks: Thin GAAP margin (4.3%) and a weak 12-month record; the re-rating could stall if industrial demand softens.
targets.exit_if: The share closes below its 200-day average, or the gain over the S&P 500 ETF since purchase falls below +5 points.

targets.name: Marathon Petroleum
targets.thesis: Now my only refiner: P/E of 7.3, 20% free-cash-flow yield and heavy buybacks, while tight fuel supply supports margins.
targets.risks: Refining margins are falling, and the share is down 21% in a month.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 22% above), or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase.

targets.name: Viatris
targets.thesis: A cheap generic-drug maker paying down debt, with a 9.1% free-cash-flow yield; it is 3.5% under its high, and its low volatility suits a defensive role.
targets.risks: High net debt (50% of mcap) and GAAP losses; generic price erosion could return.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or debt reduction stalls.

targets.name: Fortinet
targets.thesis: Network security with a 29% net margin, 20% revenue growth and net cash; after a 31% drawdown, the P/E of about 44 is more reasonable for the quality.
targets.risks: Volatility of 123% shows the market does not trust its growth outlook after the October results.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now only 1% above), or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase.

targets.name: NetApp
targets.thesis: Data storage tied to AI demand at a P/E of 24 with a 4.9% free-cash-flow yield and net cash; Q2 FY27 results are confirmed for December 1.
targets.risks: Hardware stocks are in a sharp selloff, and the share is down 18.6% in a month.
targets.exit_if: Q2 results or guidance disappoint, or it closes below its 200-day average (now 10% above).

targets.name: Keysight Technologies
targets.thesis: Test and measurement for AI and networking, with 25.5% revenue growth and record orders; fiscal Q4 results are confirmed for after the close on November 19.
targets.risks: A weak fiscal 2027 outlook would add to an 11% gap under its 200-day average during the hardware selloff.
targets.exit_if: The fiscal 2027 outlook implies revenue growth slowing below 10%, or the share keeps falling after results.

targets.name: Morgan Stanley
targets.thesis: Wealth-management fees plus a recovery in dealmaking: 16% revenue growth, a 25.5% margin and a P/E of 14; my only financials holding against a 12.7% index weight.
targets.risks: It is 7% below its 200-day average, and a deeper market drop would hurt trading and deal fees.
targets.exit_if: It falls more than 15% below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 10 points since purchase.

targets.name: Illumina, Inc.
targets.thesis: Q3 beat estimates and the company raised guidance, with a 20% margin and net cash; the 22% monthly pullback still leaves the share 16% above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: Revenue growth is only 6%, and the share has not recovered after the November 17 Jefferies talk.
targets.exit_if: It drops below its 200-day average, or trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase.

fill_rule: the Interactive Brokers demo account's fills at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday, 16:00 New York); if the broker cannot be reached, simulated at that day's Lang & Schwarz session end, mid +/- 0.05%
rules: Paper money: $100,000 at the start, in US dollars.
Only S&P 500 companies; 10 to 15 of them.
At most 10% in one company, at least 3% in each one held; cash up to 20%.
At most 3 companies in or out per decision.
Claude decides twice a week: Wednesday evening and Saturday morning.
Orders go to an Interactive Brokers demo account and fill at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday); the site records those fills: same shares, same prices.
Whole shares only, as at the broker.
Interactive Brokers' commission on each order ($1 when a fill has to be simulated); results shown before tax and after a 26% tax if sold.
No short selling, no leverage, no options, no crypto.
